subject: Film & Cinema
title: Pre-Cinema Animation Devices
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pre-Cinema Animation Devices usable.

hook.text: Before films existed, spinning discs and flickering lamps created animation in living rooms.

buildup.text: The zoetrope, thaumatrope, and phenakistoscope were Victorian toys that created motion illusions.

discovery.text: These devices proved that sequential images could simulate life — the foundation of all cinema.

twist.text: They were sold as parlor tricks. Nobody imagined they'd lead to a billion-dollar industry.

climax.text: Every animated film today traces its ancestry to spinning cardboard discs.

punchline.text: A toy invented an art form.

quiz.question: What was the zoetrope?
options: A spinning device that created the illusion of motion from sequential images
